mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 240 signals persistent inflation requiring restrictive monetary policy, suppressing equity valuations and generating negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 240.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, driving corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of HOUST growth and RSAFS increase fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate above 5.0% indicates weak labor market conditions that suppress consumer spending and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.0.

mechanism_narrative: Monthly job growth exceeding 100,000 (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 100 signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls below 100.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent housing starts growth (HOUST) and quarterly GDP expansion (GDPC1 > 1.5%) indicate broad economic strength that drives equity market performance, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of HOUST growth and GDPC1 above 1.5% fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 240) combined with low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) creates monetary policy uncertainty that depresses equity valuations, generating negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 240 and FEDFUNDS is below 0.5.
